memory_update.text: MKSI should be tracked as a US-listed underfollowed substrate/process-chemistry candidate because Atotech maps directly to package substrate copper processes, plating, via filling, and advanced packaging process control.
CAMT should be tracked as a yield-inspection beneficiary of HBM/chiplet/advanced-packaging complexity, especially if order disclosures continue to reference tier-1 OSATs and HBM manufacturers.

PDFS is a lower-attention software/data platform hypothesis for advanced-packaging yield orchestration; survival in later layers requires customer-specific evidence tied to OSAT, packaging, or HBM/chiplet workflows.

AMKR is best used as a reference demand/customer anchor for this node, not as the underfollowed alpha lane, because it is a visible OSAT advanced-packaging provider rather than a hidden substrate/material supplier.

Most direct ABF substrate and insulating-film leaders are not clean US-listed common stocks; next pass should separately map OTC/foreign listings such as Ajinomoto, Ibiden, Unimicron, Shinko, Kinsus, AT&S, and MEC if the mandate allows non-US primary listings.
ESI should be tracked as the most size-filter-compatible US-listed specialty-chemistry candidate for IC substrates, copper adhesion, RDL, copper pillar, TSV, and wafer-level packaging materials.

MKSI should be tracked as a larger but still relevant Atotech-enabled process chemistry/equipment candidate for package substrate manufacturing, copper activation, metallization, plating, and laser drilling.
ONTO should be tracked as an advanced-packaging yield-control equipment candidate tied to HBM, package inspection, 3D metrology, lithography, and factory analytics.

US-listed pure-play ABF substrate exposure appears limited; the investable US universe for this node is more likely in adjacent wet chemistry, metallization, inspection/metrology, process-control software, and OSAT pull-through.

PDF Solutions (PDFS) was not included due to the four-candidate limit, but remains a watch-list candidate for process data, yield analytics, and semiconductor supply-chain orchestration across fabless, foundry, OSAT, and test operations.

MKSI should remain in the underfollowed discovery lane for US-listed advanced packaging substrate/material exposure because Atotech maps to package substrate chemistry and electroplating, but materiality must be verified in segment disclosures.
CAMT is a yield-gate candidate rather than a substrate/material supplier; include when the funnel allows inspection/metrology bottlenecks tied to advanced packaging and HBM.
PDFS is a low-attention software/data hypothesis for advanced packaging yield orchestration; survival requires evidence of OSAT/foundry/advanced-packaging adoption and AI/HBM-specific relevance.
AMKR is best treated as a reference OSAT/customer/integration gate for the substrate/material node, not as a pure underfollowed materials candidate.

The purest substrate and material suppliers cited in the external context appear mostly non-US-listed or not clean US common-stock exposures, creating a US-listed coverage gap that pushes the discovery lane toward chemistry, inspection/metrology, OSAT, and yield software proxies.

The purest ABF-film, copper-bonding chemistry, and FC-BGA substrate chokepoints cited in the evidence are mostly outside clean US common-stock listings; US-listed exposure is mostly second-order through packaging capacity, chemistry/equipment, metrology, and yield software.

MKSI should remain on the advanced-packaging substrates/materials watchlist because Atotech provides package-substrate and semiconductor wet-process/plating/surface-treatment technologies, making it one of the more direct US-listed process-chemistry proxies.

AMKR is a capacity and integration proxy rather than a substrate/material supplier; it should be tracked for AI advanced packaging revenue, domestic packaging ramp execution, customer concentration, and substrate/material procurement risk.

PDFS is a weaker but potentially underappreciated software/data candidate; it needs evidence that advanced packaging, OSAT, assembly, and test analytics are driving durable growth rather than generic semiconductor software demand.
Future Layer 2 work should separate four distinct public-market mappings: physical substrate makers, ABF/surface-chemistry suppliers, packaging-capacity integrators, and yield-enablement vendors.

node: Advanced packaging substrates, ABF-style insulating materials, and copper-bonding chemistry
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the substrate/material/yield layer below AI accelerators and HBM. Because the most direct ABF substrate and specialty film leaders are mostly non-US-listed or OTC/non-primary listings, the strongest US-listed mapping is second-order: OSAT advanced packaging capacity, substrate/process-chemistry suppliers, inspection/metrology, and yield-data platforms. The underfollowed lane is led by MKSI, CAMT, and PDFS; AMKR is included as a reference anchor because it is a direct advanced-packaging service provider and potential beneficiary/customer of substrate and bonding-material constraints. This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around the advanced-packaging substrate/materials chokepoint. The strongest US-listed discovery candidates are not true ABF substrate makers; rather, they sit in copper plating, adhesion, wet chemistry, inspection/metrology, and process-control layers that can affect package substrate yield and advanced-packaging ramp speed. Element Solutions and MKS/Atotech are the most directly tied to copper chemistry and IC substrate process materials. Onto Innovation is a yield-control equipment candidate for HBM and advanced packaging. Amkor is included as a reference/context anchor because it is a US-listed advanced-packaging OSAT whose capacity expansion may pull demand for substrates, chemistry, metrology, and process control. Layer 1B expansion found a US-listed discovery lane around the substrate/material chokepoint, but the best US-listed names are mostly second-order rather than pure ABF substrate makers
